FAQ

Your questions, answered honestly

The bail system is confusing. We hear the same concerns every day — here's the truth.

How does the bail bond process work?

You call us with the name of the person in custody and the jail they are being held in. We confirm the bail amount, explain the cost and the paperwork before you commit to anything, then post the bond with the facility. The jail processes the release on its own timeline — typically 2 to 8 hours.

How much does a bail bond cost in California?

The premium is 10% of the bail amount and it is regulated by the State of California. On a $20,000 bail, the premium is $2,000. Any agency quoting a different rate should be questioned — and there should never be hidden fees on top.

How do I know if a bail bond company is legitimate?

Every California bail agent holds a license issued by the Department of Insurance, and you can verify it yourself on cdoi.ca.gov. Ours are CA Bail License #1841440 and CA CPA License #101195 — both linked at the top of this page so you can check before you call.

Are bail bond services available 24/7?

Yes. Arrests do not keep business hours, and neither do we. You reach a licensed bail specialist directly — nights, weekends and holidays included — not a call center or an answering service.

What information do I need to start the process?

Ideally the full name of the person arrested, the jail or city of arrest, the bail amount and the charge. If you only have a name, call anyway — we will look up the rest together.

Do you offer payment plans if I can't pay 10% upfront?

Yes. We offer flexible payment plans and will walk through the options with you before anything is signed. Tell us what is realistic for your family and we will tell you honestly what we can do.

I had a bad experience with another bail company. How are you different?

The most common complaints we hear are unanswered phones, surprise fees and pressure to sign quickly. When you call Sunset you speak with a specialist directly, the 10% premium is stated up front, and we explain every step before you commit to anything. We also stay with the case through court appearances.
